result.title: MEDALLION: Manifold Embedding Distillation and Attributions for Low-dimensional Latent InterpretatiON
result.summary: Dimensionality reduction is widely used to visualize high-dimensional data and guide scientific discovery, yet interpreting which original features contribute to low-dimensional representations remains challenging, particularly for black-box methods such as t-SNE and UMAP. We introduce \textbf{MEDALLION} (Manifold Embedding Distillation and Attributions for Low-dimensional Latent InterpretatiON), a novel framework for interpreting low-dimensional embeddings through knowledge distillation and neural feature attribution. MEDALLION distills any given embedding with a neural encoder which we explain via a broad range of existing neural feature attribution methods. Through experiments on MNIST and applications in single-cell transcriptomics, we show MEDALLION provides informative feature attributions that cast additional insights into the underlying embedding and compare its performance with existing interpretability approaches.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 MEDALLION 框架：用神经编码器蒸馏任意低维嵌入（如 t-SNE、UMAP），再借助现有神经特征归因方法解释是哪些原始特征塑造了该低维表示，并在 MNIST 与单细胞转录组数据上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 「蒸馏嵌入 + 特征归因」的流程可供核查是否能用于定位哪些视觉证据或输入维度写入 VLM 的 latent 推理状态，但原文面向降维可视化而非多模态推理，迁移性需自行判断。
